events.title: Hiram Bingham Rediscovers Machu Picchu
events.description: American explorer Hiram Bingham, guided by local villagers, reached the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu in the Peruvian Andes and brought it to international attention.
events.significance: The find drew worldwide interest to Inca civilization and made Machu Picchu one of the most famous archaeological sites in the world, later designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

events.title: Apollo 11 Returns to Earth
events.description: The Apollo 11 command module Columbia splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, bringing astronauts Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins home after the first crewed Moon landing.
events.significance: The safe return completed the mission and fulfilled President Kennedy's goal of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to Earth before the end of the 1960s.

events.title: Treaty of Lausanne Signed
events.description: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed in Switzerland between Turkey and the Allied powers, including Britain, France, Italy, Japan, Greece and Romania, settling the conflict that began in World War I.
events.significance: It superseded the Treaty of Sèvres, recognized the sovereignty of the new Republic of Turkey, and established its modern borders.

events.title: Birth of Alexandre Dumas
events.description: French writer Alexandre Dumas, author of The Three Musketeers and The Count of Monte Cristo, was born in Villers-Cotterêts, France.
events.significance: Dumas became one of the most widely read French authors, and his adventure novels helped define the historical romance genre and remain popular worldwide.

events.title: US Supreme Court Rules in United States v. Nixon
events.description: The US Supreme Court unanimously ruled that President Richard Nixon had to turn over the subpoenaed White House tape recordings related to the Watergate scandal.
events.significance: The ruling limited the scope of executive privilege and led to Nixon's resignation on August 9, 1974.
